title: Pioneer POC Kickoff: Ops Checklist and Acceptance Guidelines
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the kickoff checklist and measurable acceptance criteria for the Pioneer Retail POC. The objective: validate Redwood Inference hosted + dedicated hybrid for real-time product search ranking and conversational product assistant with the Pioneer dataset and sample traffic profile. The POC covers integration, throughput, latency, quality, and operational runbook validation over a 4-week engagement.

Primary objectives (what success looks like):
- Integration: Full end-to-end pipeline from Pioneer frontend to Redwood API with authenticated requests, semantic reranker hook, and embedding store connectivity; at least one automated CI flow demonstrating deploy -> smoke test.
- Latency SLOs: p50 generation latency <= 60ms, p95 <= 250ms under baseline simulated traffic (see traffic profile below).
- Throughput: Sustained 200 requests per second (RPS) across the primary route with tail latency within SLOs; burst to 400 RPS with graceful degradation and fallback configured.
- Quality: Reranker NDCG@10 improves baseline search by >= 12% on provided eval set; generative assistant passes 80% of curated prompt/intent acceptance checks.
- Cost-Efficiency: Demonstrated inference cost per 1k queries not to exceed the projected budget baseline (internal cost model) by more than 15% after tuning (batching, quantization recommendations applied).
- Operational readiness: Alerting, tracing, and per-request cost attribution visible in Redwood Console for the routes used by Pioneer.

POC Scope:
- In scope: Hosted API integration, model selection and benchmarking (two candidate open models + Redwood-verified variant), dedicated capacity smoke tests, prefix/KV cache configuration, basic rollout/canary test.
- Out of scope: Full-on private on-prem deployment, training or fine-tuning of base models, long-term data retention or compliance packaging (can be scoped in later).

Traffic and dataset profile for tests:
- Sample traffic: 70% short chat messages (user Q/A), 20% reranker batch requests, 10% embedding lookup.
- Payload sizes: typical user message 40-120 tokens, max 512 tokens for targeted stress test.
- Synthetic load plan: ramp 0 -> 200 RPS over 10 minutes; hold 60 minutes; spike to 400 RPS for 5 minutes; observe metrics for 30 minutes after spike.

Acceptance criteria (hard pass/fail checkpoints):
1) End-to-end functional smoke test (must pass):
   - Login/auth flow works with API key/managed token, sample assistant response returned with correct JSON schema for 20 consecutive requests.
   - Reranker returns ranked ids in expected format for provided eval queries.
2) Performance gates (must meet all three):
   - p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 250ms during the sustained 200 RPS window.
   - No more than 1% 5xx errors during sustained window.
   - CPU/GPU utilization for dedicated nodes not exceeding 85% sustained (to avoid saturation) during the hold period.
3) Quality gates (quantitative):
   - Reranker NDCG@10 >= baseline * 1.12 on the Pioneer eval set.
   - Conversational intent accuracy >= 80% on the curated 50-prompt acceptance set (binary pass/fail judged by product owner).
4) Reliability and fallback validation:
   - Canary rollout to 10% of traffic succeeds for 30 minutes without error rate increase; automatic fallback triggers in less than 90s when error threshold is reached in a controlled failure test.
5) Observability and cost reporting:
   - Traces link from frontend request ID to Redwood Console route spans for >= 95% of sampled requests.
   - Per-request cost estimate and token breakdown available in the Console for the test routes.

Operational checklist (pre-kickoff to week 1 items):
- Pre-kickoff:
  - Exchange API credentials and IP allowlist with Pioneer security team (owner: Alicia).
  - Pioneer provides sample dataset (50k product descriptions + 2k eval queries) and sample frontend request format (owner: Pioneer eng).
  - Confirm compliance/non-PII status of dataset.
  - Create JIRA epic and tape to Confluence doc (linked artifact above).
- Day 0 (kickoff session):
  - 1-hour technical kickoff: participants, goals, timeline, risk review.
  - Share test accounts and ephemeral tokens for initial smoke.
- Week 0-1:
  - Integration sprint: implement API client, map request/response schemas, initial smoke test by end of week 1.
  - Model benchmarking: run three 10-minute benchmarks for each candidate model variant with baseline traffic generator. Record latency/throughput/cost.
- Week 2:
  - Performance tuning: enable batching/cache settings advised by Redwood Optimize; try int8 quantized variant on dedicated nodes if available; iterate.
  - Run full synthetic load plan and document metrics.
- Week 3-4:
  - Quality validation: run reranker eval and conversational acceptance checks, remediate prompt engineering mismatches.
  - Canary rollout and fallback test; validation of alerts and SLO dashboards.
  - Final acceptance run and sign-off meeting.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Pioneer (customer): dataset, product acceptance owner, frontend engineer for integration testing.
- Redwood Solutions Eng (owner: Alicia Chen): POC lead, integration checkpoints, acceptance facilitator.
- Performance lead: Marcus Patel — benchmarking, load plans, tuning recommendations.
- Observability & SRE liaison: Leah Gómez — dashboard setup, alert rules, tracing sampling.
- Account Exec / CSM: Priya Nair — commercial boundary, contract questions, go/no-go coordination.

Risk register (top items):
- Dataset contains unexpected PII -> mitigation: pause tests, run redaction pipeline, re-evaluate scope.
- Model quality below threshold -> mitigation: try alternate model family or reranker-only architecture, tighten prompt engineering, extend POC by 1 week if agreed.
- Infrastructure cost runaway during stress -> mitigation: set hard account-level spend cap; use autoscale policies with strict upper bounds.

Sign-off template (post final acceptance run):
- Pioneer product owner: name, title, signature (email ok), date.
- Redwood POC lead (Alicia Chen): name, signature, date.
- Notes: any deferred items to be captured in follow-up action plan with owners and ETA.

Open questions to resolve during kickoff:
- Pioneer: is there a preferred authentication method beyond API key (OIDC, mTLS)?
- Pioneer: acceptable window for brief service interruptions during canary fail test?
- Redwood: do we have access to a representative production-like embedding store for reranker evaluation or do we reuse the sample dataset?

Appendix: quick runbook snippets
- Smoke test curl (example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"route":"pioneer-assistant","input":"what's the best winter jacket?"}'
- Canary rollback steps:
  1) Disable route in Redwood Console -> revert to prior model alias.
  2) Confirm rollback by running 10 smoke requests.
  3) Notify Pioneer slack channel and schedule follow-up.

Next steps before kickoff meeting:
- Confirm kickoff attendees and calendar invite (owner: Alicia).
- Pioneer to upload sample dataset to shared S3 or GDrive stub with read permissions for Redwood eng.
- Redwood to provision dedicated test pool and share estimated cost delta for the POC (performance lead: Marcus).

Document revision notes: initial draft 2025-11-03 by Alicia Chen; performance additions and ramp plan updated 2025-11-14 by Marcus Patel.
